ai.description: The Himalayan Krait reaches 1.2–1.5m. It is black with narrow, white transverse bands and a distinct vertebral ridge. The subcaudal scales are entire, and the head is slightly distinct from the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Himalayan Krait is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of narrow, white, chevron-shaped crossbands that point forward, contrasting with the bands of other kraits.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Krait inhabits dense, humid subtropical forests and mountain slopes in the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Krait is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small snakes, lizards, and amphibians among leaf litter and rocky terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Himalayan Krait is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–14 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, with eggs often hatching in late summer or autumn.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Krait occurs in Northeast India (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
